decision.reason: Goose sends resolved HTTP credentials before it can verify the expected MCP surface identity, and its mutable permission model is not an immutable approval boundary.

local_observation.provenance: observed local executable only; not accepted as official release-artifact proof

goose_semantics.extension_name_normalization: lowercase; remove whitespace; preserve ASCII alphanumeric, hyphen, and underscore; replace each remaining character with underscore
goose_semantics.secret_resolution_order: resolve URI and headers, build authenticated client, send initialize, then retain returned serverInfo

required_gates.evidence: The installed executable was observed and hashed, but no matching official platform-asset digest was acquired and verified.
Pinned source qualifies remote tools as normalized-extension__server-tool; the two canonical extension names normalize distinctly.
Pinned source enforces available_tools during enumeration and before dispatch; repository regressions reject empty allowlists because Goose treats empty as allow all.

An isolated v1.45.0 run proves a missing header secret prevents any MCP receipt while Goose continues without the extension. A configured secret is expanded only in memory and was absent from the temporary root after the run; this fail-open extension loss still cannot support authenticated Zabin operation.

A loopback hostile server receives the expanded bearer on its first initialize request and only then returns serverInfo; exact release source confirms server_info is retained after client.serve initializes.

Digest-pinned config/permission.rs checks always_allow, ask_before, then never_allow. Source-parity and native approve-mode regressions place one principal in all three lists; Goose invokes it without prompting, proving always_allow wins while runtime state remains mutable.
No immutable externally brokered approval contract is documented for unattended Goose runs.
Hook failures and timeouts are logged and execution continues; hooks cannot be the mandatory authorization or startup identity boundary.
CLI recipe trust and workspace trust are not mandatory native gates; MCP instructions are accepted into agent context.
Native Developer and stdio extensions execute with Goose process authority, and MCP roots are advisory.

The optional native regression removes its exact temporary GOOSE_PATH_ROOT and recorder, proves no expanded bearer residue, and observes no MCP delete operation. Goose ordinarily creates session/project/log artifacts, so active install cleanup and drift still require a later transactional implementation.

blocking_reasons: Expected MCP surface identity cannot be authenticated before bearer-header release.
Secret-safe generated Authorization-header indirection is not a documented stable contract.
The default autonomous mode bypasses approvals and persistent permission state is mutable.
Hook failure and timeout behavior is fail open for the required enforcement boundary.
There is no mandatory CLI workspace/recipe trust boundary or general native sandbox.
Official platform artifact integrity, active-install cleanup, and drift evidence are incomplete.
reevaluation_requirements: Pin and verify the exact official platform artifact digest.
Prove bearer indirection, missing-secret containment, and redaction without persisting a token value.
Authenticate the expected logical surface, protocol, and inventory before releasing or exchanging its credential.
Prove exact non-empty per-surface allowlists, qualified collision isolation, forbidden dispatch rejection, and zero forbidden server receipts.
Enforce approve mode and mutually exclusive per-tool permissions below mutable user configuration.
Provide an authorization and startup identity boundary whose failures and timeouts deny execution rather than relying on Goose hooks.
Provide mandatory recipe/workspace trust and an enforceable process/filesystem isolation boundary.
Prove transactional install, cleanup, rollback, and source/target/policy/version/inventory drift handling.
